issues.legal_issue: An appellate court deciding whether to stay execution of a money decree may accept adequate security instead of requiring a cash deposit when the circumstances warrant that exercise of discretion.
material_facts: A public body performing public utility functions appealed a money decree and sought a stay of execution pending appeal.
It pleaded financial difficulty and a need to retain funds for its public services, and offered security instead of depositing cash.
The appeal raised a prima facie strong case for consideration on its merits.
The decree-holder did not contend that the amount would be unrecoverable if the appeal failed.
The public body furnished immovable-property security to the satisfaction of the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court should have permitted security instead of insisting on a cash deposit; the orders requiring the deposit were set aside and the stay was made subject to the furnished property security.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XLI Rules 1(3) and 5(5) of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appellate court has discretion to require either deposit of the disputed amount or security it considers fit as a condition of staying execution. That discretion must be exercised judicially and according to the circumstances, not arbitrarily. Execution of a money decree is ordinarily not stayed because payment generally does not cause irreparable injury and restitution is available if the appeal succeeds, but a stay may be granted in an appropriate case. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: appeal_from_money_decree_seeking_execution_stay and appellant_performs_public_utility_functions and appellant_needs_funds_for_public_services and appeal_has_prima_facie_strong_case and decree_holder_does_not_dispute_recoverability and adequate_property_security_is_furnished

predicates.appeal_from_money_decree_seeking_executi: The appellant sought a stay of execution while appealing a decree requiring payment of money.
predicates.appellant_performs_public_utility_functi: The appellant is a public body that performs public utility functions.
predicates.appellant_needs_funds_for_public_service: The appellant showed that it needed to retain funds to carry out its public services.
predicates.appeal_has_prima_facie_strong_case: The appellant presented a prima facie strong case for the appeal to be heard on its merits.
predicates.decree_holder_does_not_dispute_recoverab: The decree-holder did not claim that the amount would be unrecoverable if the appeal failed.
predicates.adequate_property_security_is_furnished: The appellant furnished immovable-property security that the trial court found satisfactory.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a money decree seeks a stay, the appellant performs public utility functions, needs funds for public services, has a prima facie strong appeal, recoverability is not disputed, and adequate property security is furnished, the stay is conditioned on that security rather than a cash deposit.
